job_description_info.job_description:
# Machine Learning Engineer – Customer Support AI

**Company:** Quillstone Payments (fictional name; card-payment and business-tools provider)
**Location:** Hamburg, Germany (office-first)
**Team:** AI team within Customer Operations

## About the team

The Customer Operations organisation wants merchants to get help quickly and without friction. The AI team builds models and assistants that answer merchant questions, route tickets and help support agents. You will work with backend engineers, data scientists and product managers to take ideas from prototype to production.

## What you will do

- Build, deploy and operate AI and machine learning systems used by the support organisation
- Maintain pipelines for data processing, training and serving
- Fine-tune and evaluate models, including language models, for accuracy and cost
- Prepare and clean large text datasets
- Apply normal engineering discipline: version control, CI/CD and automated tests
- Integrate ML components into the wider product with other engineering teams

## Requirements

- Degree in machine learning, computer science or a related engineering field
- At least four years of experience as a machine learning engineer shipping ML or AI systems to production
- Experience with AI products such as chat assistants or retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)
- Software engineering skills for production systems: model serving, monitoring, data versioning
- Experience with a major cloud provider (AWS, GCP or Azure)
- Strong Python; familiarity with MLOps and orchestration tools such as MLflow, Kubeflow, Airflow or an LLM-observability tool
- Experience with feature engineering and data ingestion pipelines

## Benefits

- Annual learning budget, employee share programme and company pension contribution
- Relocation support and subsidised meals
- Sabbatical after several years of service

company_info.company_description:
Quillstone Payments is a privately held financial services company founded in 2013 and headquartered in Hamburg, Germany. It builds payment and business tools for small merchants, including card terminals, a point-of-sale app and business accounts. It also offers a personal account for merchants’ customers. The company serves several million merchants across Europe and the Americas, with around 2,500 employees of many nationalities working in approximately 20 offices.

Quillstone’s culture emphasises **ownership, teamwork and learning from mistakes**. Teams own their services and have autonomy to solve merchants’ problems, guided by shared principles rather than heavy processes. The company values pragmatism, humility, candid feedback and openly shared context.

Quillstone is **office-first**: employees generally work side by side, with teams agreeing on some flexible days. Its learning culture includes training budgets, peer feedback, internal tech talks and development plans reviewed twice a year. The company also offers relocation support for many roles, supports local business education projects and publishes an annual inclusion report.

cover_letter_history.content:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am applying for the Machine Learning Engineer – Customer Support AI role at Quillstone Payments. With more than five years of experience in natural language processing, document classification, and taking ML models from research and prototyping into production, I would welcome the opportunity to apply this background to systems that help merchants and support agents.

At Slavonica Document AI, I developed a document classification model that achieved 94% accuracy across 23 classes and fine-tuned BERTić and XLM-R for named entity recognition in Croatian documents. I also introduced MLflow for experiment tracking and model registration, and established production model-quality and data-drift monitoring for our deployed Python-based services. Our models are delivered as FastAPI services in Docker containers on Azure ML and App Service. I use Python to build these services and Git for version control.

My earlier work at Baranjska kreditna banka included classifying topics in customer complaint texts. I also built and annotated a corpus of Croatian legal texts as a research project assistant. Alongside my professional work, I am pursuing doctoral research in named entity recognition and hold a master’s degree in computer engineering.

I would welcome the chance to discuss how my experience building, deploying, operating, and monitoring NLP models in production from research through production could contribute to your Customer Operations AI team. Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,
Petra Zlatarić-Novosel

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is concise, professional, and well structured. It presents relevant evidence rather than repeating the CV, including the 94% classification result, transformer fine-tuning, MLflow, model serving, Azure deployment, and production monitoring. The progression from current production work to earlier text-classification and research experience is clear. Its main weakness is that some claims are broad or repetitive, and it does not explicitly connect the candidate’s experience to the engineering practices and customer-support use cases emphasized in the role.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is ATS-friendly: it uses standard headings and plain text, contains no problematic tables or graphics, and includes strong supported keywords such as Python, NLP, model serving, MLflow, model registry, monitoring, FastAPI, Docker, Azure ML, App Service, Git, and production. AI screening probability is moderate to strong for the requirements supported by the candidate’s background. Screening may be weaker for the exact requirements and phrases not evidenced in the candidate information, including chat assistants or RAG, feature engineering, data ingestion pipelines, CI/CD, automated testing, orchestration beyond MLflow, and data versioning. These should not be added unless they are factually supported.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The letter aligns well with the role’s core production-ML responsibilities: it demonstrates NLP model development, fine-tuning, deployment, model serving, monitoring, cloud use, and progression from research to production. It also connects reasonably well to customer-support work through the candidate’s experience classifying customer complaint topics. The candidate’s computer engineering degree, Python experience, Azure experience, and MLflow use are supported. Gaps in the candidate material include demonstrated experience with chat assistants or RAG, feature engineering, and data ingestion pipelines. The candidate material also does not clearly establish at least four years specifically as a machine learning engineer shipping systems to production, although it does establish more than five years of broader NLP and machine-learning experience. The letter does not provide much evidence related to teamwork, learning from mistakes, candid feedback, or service ownership, although mentoring interns can support a limited teamwork and development connection.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL ALIGNMENT/CLARITY IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the second paragraph, change “I also introduced MLflow for experiment tracking and model registration” to “I also introduced MLflow for experiment tracking and the model registry.” This uses the exact terminology supported by the CV and more closely matches the job ad’s MLOps language.
2. In the second paragraph, change “established production model-quality and data-drift monitoring for our deployed Python-based services” to “established production model-quality monitoring, including data-drift monitoring and weekly reporting, for deployed Python services.” This is more precise and reflects the candidate’s documented responsibilities.
3. In the closing paragraph, remove the repetitive phrase “in production from research through production” and replace the full sentence with: “I would welcome the chance to discuss how my experience building, deploying, operating, and monitoring NLP models could contribute to Quillstone’s Customer Operations AI team.” This eliminates repetition while retaining the strongest role-relevant terms.
4. In the third paragraph, make the customer-support relevance more explicit by changing “My earlier work at Baranjska kreditna banka included classifying topics in customer complaint texts” to “At Baranjska kreditna banka, I classified topics in customer complaint texts, giving me directly relevant experience working with support-related language data.” This remains truthful and connects the evidence to the target team.
5. Before the final paragraph, add one short sentence based on the documented mentoring experience: “I also mentor two student interns, an experience that has strengthened my collaborative approach and commitment to knowledge sharing.” This provides limited but truthful evidence relevant to the company’s teamwork and learning culture without claiming unsupported leadership or ownership.
6. In the opening paragraph, replace “systems that help merchants and support agents” with “AI systems that help support organisations classify and route customer requests and assist support agents” only if the intended phrasing is clearly presented as motivation rather than claimed prior experience. Do not state that the candidate has built assistants, routing systems, or merchant-facing products, because those experiences are not present in the candidate information.
